messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Private deploy: multi-site residency handover and networking checklist

Team / NordicBank folks —

Quick sync note as we move into the handover week for NordicBank's VPC private deployment across Frankfurt (eu) and Singapore (apac) sites. The ask from procurement + security is simple: provide a deterministic runbook that covers residency guarantees, routing failover, and the network-level controls we hand off to the customer.

I put together an initial checklist and a small diagram attached. Key items I want covered in this thread:
- IP block assignment expectations and NAT egress patterns per region
- Cross-region failover trigger (automated vs manual) and RTO/RPO targets
- KMS key residency for customer-managed encryption (who rotates keys where)
- Audit log retention and where logs live (control plane vs customer logs)
- Marketplace/partner implications for private offering (cloud partner checklist)

Action items: Laura, can you confirm the control-plane audit retention SLA we offer for private deployments? Vivek, please confirm the recommended failover policy (canary -> full) and whether we require warm standby in APAC for this customer given their SLA. Dev, please validate the networking checklist items in the attached spreadsheet — particularly BGP vs VPN options.

NordicBank — a few of these items will need your confirmation (IP ranges, firewall management scope, and preferred KMS region). Please reply inline where possible.

Attachments: residency-diagram-v2.png (diagram), networking-handover-checklist.xlsx (checklist), mcafee-scan-summary.pdf (latest host scan summary)

—
Markus Klein
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, ops@nordicbank.com
Cc: security@nordicbank.com, pm@cloudpartner.example
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy: multi-site residency handover and networking checklist

Thanks Markus — good framing. A few clarifications from my side:

- Control-plane audit retention: for Private (VPC) we provide 90 days by default in the control plane and we can extend to 365 days as a paid add-on. If NordicBank requires provider-side retention in-country, we need a private collector deployed in their VPC (adds ~2 weeks).
- Logs: operational logs (ordering, routing decisions) remain in our control plane unless customer provisions a log-forwarder. We should document the forwarder setup in the checklist (see tab "Log Forwarder").
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported. Recommend storing key material in EU for Frankfurt, and in APAC for Singapore; rotation policy can be aligned to their policy but we require an automated key access test on deploy.

I'll update the checklist with the retention options and the log-forwarder steps.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product — Private
Redwood Inference

Markus / team —

Thanks for the checklist and diagram. A couple of items from our side:

- IP space: we'll provide two /24s per region; prefer to terminate egress via our NAT gateway in Frankfurt for EU traffic.
- Failover: we prefer an automated RPO-driven failover but need a 30 minute hold window to allow graceful draining of in-flight requests for critical endpoints.
- KMS: keys must be stored in EU for EU data; Singapore key OK for APAC, but all customer key lifecycle events need to be auditable through our SIEM.

Can you confirm whether the private collector option Laura mentioned will cause any changes to latency or require additional peering? Also the mcafee-scan-summary.pdf — is that a Redwood internal scan or something we run on the appliance?

Best,

Platform Ops, NordicBank

Ola / team —

I've gone through the networking-handover-checklist.xlsx and annotated the approach matrix. Short summary:

- Preferred topologies:
  * Option A (recommended): VPC peering + BGP sessions to their transit in each region. Provides deterministic routing and avoids transit hops for EU-bound traffic.
  * Option B: IPsec VPN with active/passive pair — simpler but slower failover and higher CPU on the appliance.

- Private collector note: deploying the log-forwarder in-customer VPC requires a small container (200MB RAM) and one extra NIC. No extra cross-region peering required, but you'll want to expose the collector to the customer SIEM over TLS (mutual TLS recommended).

- McAfee scan: that was run against our marketplace appliance image; summary attached. No high severity findings.

I'll attach the checklist back with inline comments. Next step: finalize topology choice and sign the network ops runbook.

—
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the updates everyone — short confirmation from ops/infra:

- Failover policy: we will implement a staged failover: canary traffic redirected to standby region for 10 minutes with health checks; if errors persist beyond 10 minutes, escalate to full region shift. We will record the event and emit an SLO breach if effective latency/availability thresholds are hit.
- Warm standby requirement: given NordicBank's SLA, we will keep a warm standby in APAC (hot cache, preloaded models) — cost is noted in the draft commercial addendum.

Markus — please coordinate a short handover call (30 minutes) with Ola and their security lead to run through the KMS integration and collector setup. I suggest Monday 22 June, 09:00 UTC.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference
